results.correct_value: No glacier crossing on the approach to the ridge toe; glacier contact (skirting high glacial ice and an icy moat atop/near the Goode Glacier) occurs high on the route near the Southeast Peak.
results.evidence: The AAC report says the party left the North Fork Bridge Creek trail at a clearing and climbed to the toe of the northeast arete, and met an icy moat near the Southeast Peak above the Goode Glacier. Alpinist says after bivying on the ridge they scouted a path around the high glacial ice and climbed through a moat atop the Goode Glacier. So obj_haz 'on approach' and the day-2 'across the glacier' line were wrong, and seasonal_hazards' flat denial of any glacier contact was also wrong.

A third report approached via Easy Pass to the basin camp. The trailhead card/waypoint (Thunder Creek) remain valid as one of the two options.

results.fact: Cumulative gain/loss for an out-and-back route
results.correct_value: ~12,500 ft gain and ~12,500 ft loss car to car via Easy Pass (out and back)
results.evidence: One report gives 29 mi and 12,500 ft gain for the Easy Pass out-and-back; another gives 35 mi and 13,000 ft, with ~4,600 ft of gain on the day to the lake camp. The row's own itinerary totalNote already says ~12,500 ft. Day splits were made consistent with the named elevations: trailhead 3,700 + 4,600 gain - 3,100 loss = lake camp ~5,160; the summit day (lake 5,160 to 9,087 plus the Christmas Tree Col drop onto the glacier) carries the remaining 4,800 ft; day 3 reverses day 1. The per-day split is derived, the total is sourced.

results.fact: Cumulative gain/loss for an out-and-back route
results.correct_value: ~9,200 ft gain and ~9,200 ft loss (out and back from Easy Pass Trailhead)
results.evidence: The route is out and back from the Easy Pass Trailhead (3,700 ft) over Easy Pass (~6,500-6,600 ft) to a Fisher Basin camp (~4,800 ft) and the 9,087-ft summit, so loss must equal gain and the minimum from those elevations is ~8,800 ft; the itinerary's symmetric 9,200 ft fits and both 7,000 gain and 1,500 loss do not. Trip reports confirm the Easy Pass Trailhead start at 3,700 ft and the return climbing ~3,000 ft back to Easy Pass before descending the same amount; the summit elevation 9,087 ft is the catalog's agreed figure.
